title: Interac e-Transfer for Online Stores in Canada
description: Taking Interac e-Transfer in a Canadian online store: manual setup on Shopify and WooCommerce, why Square leaves it out, Autodeposit and how to match payments.
h1: Interac e-Transfer at checkout: how it works on each platform
name: Interac e-Transfer
lead: Plenty of Canadian buyers would rather send an e-Transfer than type in a card number, and the money moves straight from their bank to yours. But none of the big store platforms takes e-Transfer the way it takes a card. On each one it is a manual payment you confirm yourself, and the work is in matching money to orders.

facts.label: Shopify
facts.value: Email money transfers are a custom manual payment method, available only to merchants in Canada; you mark the order paid after accepting the transfer

facts.label: WooCommerce
facts.value: No built-in e-Transfer method; Direct Bank Transfer is the closest core option and holds orders On hold until you confirm payment

facts.label: WooCommerce request
facts.value: A request to add e-Transfer to the Stripe extension, submitted January 25, 2023, was still open

facts.label: Square
facts.value: Square's Canadian article positions its card payments as an alternative to e-Transfer; we found no Square checkout option for it

facts.label: Autodeposit
facts.value: Funds land without a login and the payer does not answer a security question

facts.label: Business limit
facts.value: Up to $25,000 per transaction, depending on the financial institution and account type

facts.label: Fees
facts.value: Set by your bank or credit union, not by Interac

facts.label: Request Money
facts.value: A business can send a payment request with an invoice number in the message; message length is limited

sections.h2: Shopify: a custom manual payment method
body: Shopify supports e-Transfer only as what it calls an email money transfer, and only for merchants in Canada. In Settings, Payments, you create a custom manual payment method, name it, and write the instructions customers see at checkout: the email address to send to and, if you do not use Autodeposit, the security question and answer. The customer places the order, the order waits unpaid, and once you accept the transfer you mark the order as paid in the admin.

Put the order number in the instructions and ask buyers to include it in the transfer message. Without it, matching a deposit from a name you do not recognize to one of a dozen pending orders becomes guesswork.

sections.h2: WooCommerce: repurpose Direct Bank Transfer or add a plugin
body: WooCommerce has no e-Transfer gateway in core, and a request on WooCommerce.com to add it to the Stripe extension has been open since early 2023. The usual workaround is the built-in Direct Bank Transfer method. You rename its title to Interac e-Transfer, replace the bank account wording with your e-Transfer email and instructions, and WooCommerce puts each order On hold until you confirm the money arrived. WooCommerce's own guidance is to check that funds have cleared before moving an order to Processing or Completed.

Plugins on WordPress.org add a dedicated e-Transfer method, and some try to match incoming transfers to orders automatically. We have not tested them for this page. If you use one, check how it handles a buyer who sends the wrong amount or forgets the order number.

sections.h2: Square: no e-Transfer option at checkout
body: Square's checkout and invoices are built around cards and wallets. Its own Canadian article argues for card payments over e-Transfer, citing fake transfers, phishing and transfer limits. We found no Square help page that adds e-Transfer to Square Online or Square Invoices. If a customer wants to pay a Square invoice by e-Transfer, you would take the money outside Square and record the invoice as paid by another method yourself.

sections.h2: Set up the receiving side first
body: Turn on Autodeposit with your business bank before you offer e-Transfer. With Autodeposit, funds land without you logging in to accept each one and buyers do not need a security question, which removes a common support email. Limits depend on your bank and account type; Interac's business page puts the ceiling at $25,000 per transaction for some accounts. Fees are set by your bank or credit union, so check your account's current pricing.

For larger orders, or anything you build an invoice for, Interac's Request Money feature lets your business send a request with the invoice number in the message. The buyer pays from the request, which gets you the amount and reference you asked for instead of whatever the buyer typed.

The risk with e-Transfer is not fraud by the buyer so much as orders that ship before money arrives, or money that sits unmatched. Decide who checks the inbox or bank each morning, how long an unpaid order stays open before it is cancelled, and what you do when an amount is a few dollars short. Write that into the checkout instructions so buyers know the order holds until payment lands.

stepsHeading: Add e-Transfer to a Shopify store

steps.name: Turn on Autodeposit
steps.text: Register your business email for Autodeposit with your bank so transfers land without a security question.

steps.name: Create the method
steps.text: In Shopify, go to Settings, Payments, and choose Create custom payment method under manual payment methods.

steps.name: Write the instructions
steps.text: Name it Interac e-Transfer and give the email address, the amount rule and a request to put the order number in the message.

steps.name: Activate and test
steps.text: Activate it, place a small order, send the e-Transfer and mark the order paid once it arrives.

checklist: Autodeposit is on for the address shown at checkout
Checkout instructions ask for the order number in the message
Unpaid e-Transfer orders do not release to fulfilment automatically
Someone checks deposits against open orders every business day
Your cancel rule for unpaid orders is written down

faqs.q: Can an e-Transfer be charged back like a card?
faqs.a: Interac says payments collected through its Bulk Receivables requests are guaranteed with no chargebacks. For ordinary transfers, ask your bank how it handles one sent in error or under dispute.
No. On Shopify, e-Transfer is a manual payment method you confirm yourself.

faqs.q: What does it cost to receive an e-Transfer?
faqs.a: Your bank or credit union sets the fee. Check the current price on your business account.
